speaker: Dan Driscoll; Brig. Gen. Matt Ross; Col. Anna Scott (British Army)
role: SecArmy; Director JIATF-401; British Army advisor
venue: US-UK Joint Declaration of Intent on C-UAS data standards
quote: Vendors who adopt these standards will find a more direct path to their capabilities.
points: Common C-UAS data formats for allied sensor fusion and data sharing.
Five more nations to follow; up to 25 countries able to buy from the JIATF-401 marketplace by summer 2026.
Marketplace listings will require compliance with the data standard.
um_relevance: UM's interceptor must output tracks and engagement status in the JIATF-401 / US-UK data standard and integrate with Lattice. That compliance is the price of entry to both US and allied buyers.

speaker: Defense Innovation Unit / DCMA
quote: (Blue UAS list moved to DCMA; new portal launched)
points: Blue UAS list now run by DCMA (bluelist.dcma.mil) under Hegseth's 'small UAS domain dominance by end of 2027' directive.
Framework: 81 vetted companies, 39 platforms, 165 cleared components; focus on Group 1-2.
um_relevance: UM's interceptor is itself a UAS. Building from Blue-cleared, NDAA-compliant components (and later pursuing Blue listing) removes a procurement objection.

speaker: Jason Mayes
venue: Interview with The War Zone (historical baseline)
quote: They're not appropriate for the homeland.
points: Listed as appropriate at home: EW/cyber, GPS/RF jamming (with limits), passive detection, net or streamer-launching drones, link hijacking.
Excluded: lasers, HPM, missiles, guns, and kinetic interceptors like Coyote.
Net drones work like a goalie but cannot keep up with 150-200+ mph FPV drones.
um_relevance: HISTORICAL BASELINE (Oct 2024). Since then NORTHCOM's own Flyaway Kit includes Anduril's Anvil low-collateral kinetic interceptor, and JIATF-401 asks for non-explosive kinetic interceptors for homeland use. Capture is no longer the only approved airborne effector. UM's wedge narrows from 'only legal option' to 'lowest-collateral option that also defeats RF-silent drones'.
